title: Wearing the Shoes of Someone Who Passed Away

chapters.title: Introduction and Sefer Hasidim
chapters.about: Questions about using or giving away clothing and shoes of a deceased person and reference to Sefer Hasidim.

chapters.title: Sefer Hasidim on Dangerous Sedaka
chapters.about: Rabbi Uda Hasid's statement about not giving items of danger as Sedaka.

chapters.title: Customs in Baghdad and Remez in Debarim
chapters.about: Customs cited by the Ben Ish Hai, Hacham Ovadia Yosef, and a textual hint in Debarim noted by Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky.

chapters.title: Gemara in Masekhet Hullin
chapters.about: Talmudic passage in Masekhet Hullin 94a concerning leather from an unslaughtered dead animal.

chapters.title: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein on Contagious Disease
chapters.about: Explanation linking the concern to contagious disease and whether sanitizing or timing of wear affects the ruling.

chapters.title: Gemara in Masekhet Berachot on Dreams
chapters.about: Talmudic discussion in Masekhet Berachot 57b regarding dreams of a deceased person taking shoes.

chapters.title: Leather Shoes, Slippers, and Giving Sedaka
chapters.about: Distinctions for non-leather shoes and slippers according to Rabbi Moshe Sternbach and practical guidance on giving items as Sedaka.

claims: “Rabbi Moshe Sternbach regarding contagious disease and non-leather footwear” - Rabbi Sternbach is only cited regarding non-leather footwear and slippers, not contagious disease.
summary: Rabbi Harari examines the custom and halakhic discussions concerning whether one may wear or give away the clothing and shoes of someone who passed away. He reviews sources beginning with Sefer Hasidim, a textual hint in Debarim noted by Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky, and Talmudic passages in Masekhet Hullin and Masekhet Berachot. He also addresses explanations offered by Rabbi Moshe Feinstein, Hacham Ovadia Yosef, and Rabbi Moshe Sternbach regarding contagious disease and non-leather footwear.
